title: Jensen Huang’s 700,000% Return Magnifies Nvidia Succession Risks
title_cn: Jensen Huang’s 700,000% Return Magnifies Nvidia Succession Risks
summary: The office of Nvidia’s Jensen Huang has an unusual setup: The chief executive officer sits at an enormous oval desk facing his lieutenants, with room for more employees in stadium seating behind them. The arrangement — created as part of Nvidia’s headquarters in Santa Clara, California — is purpose-built to suit how Huang runs the company. Though it’s not uncommon to see cultlike tech CEOs who obsess over details, Huang is in a class of his own. He has led the business since its very beginning 33 years ago, the longest such run in Silicon Valley. And even as Nvidia grew into one of the world’s most powerful companies — with a stock return of more than 700,000% — there’s still no one designated to potentially replace him. title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Anthropic Targets $1.4 Trillion Valuation
title_cn: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Anthropic Targets $1.4 Trillion Valuation
summary:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF

Anthropic  is seeking a valuation of about $1.4 trillion in its initial public offering, a bid to make history as the first frontier artificial intelligence lab to go public. The Claude chatbot maker and its co-founders are looking to raise as much as $90.4 billion in the IPO and a private placement. The base offering would raise up to $64.4 billion, with shares marketed for $70 to $78 each, according to a filing on Tuesday with the US Securities and Exchange Commission. Anthropic is offering 801.4 million shares, while backers are selling 23.6 million shares.

On today’s episode:

Anthony Hughes, Bloomberg News Equity Capital Market Reporter
Matthew Luzzetti, Chief US Economist, Deutsche Bank
Dave Lee, Bloomberg Opinion Columnist
Melissa Smith, President & CEO, Wex (Source: Bloomberg)

Gallego also calls for scrutiny of whether outside influence played a role in Nvidia’s push to loosen chip export controls on China, and says the crypto industry will have to talk to returning Sen.
